context:
In the Arathi Basin battleground, computer-run stand-in squads (small groups of three or six characters that fill out each side) do not choose their own way. They walk a network of fixed roads that join the two home bases and the five bases between them: Stables, Farm, Gold Mine, Lumber Mill and Blacksmith. Wherever roads meet is a crossing. At a crossing, a squad takes any road except the one it just arrived by, and the choices are dealt out in turn, so successive squads spread evenly over every road without any randomness.

Because the rule never asks which road is "nearer the enemy", nothing in it tells a squad to stop. A squad keeps passing through crossings until something else interrupts it. That could be a base to capture or to stay and guard, a fight with enemy players or squads, or arrival at the enemy side's home base, which is where the roads from their side end. If the enemy's home counts as an end, squads that reach it stop there. That makes it a clear goal, but squads pile up and idle there. If it is not an end, they keep taking the rule's roads, turn round at the home and head back across the map. That keeps the match moving, but squads would never settle at their goal.

The Basin also has a river that runs from the Blacksmith. It is not a road and is deliberately not walkable. The Lumber Mill sits on a cliff above the river. A stand-in only ends up in the river by accident, knocked back, cycloned (spun helpless) or feared (forced to run) off an edge. A stand-in that lands there walks out to the nearest point of the nearest road, carries on from the first crossing it reaches, and joins the first group it meets. In effect it is "recovered" back onto the roads. The map has one more place to decide: the Lumber Mill cliff. If a fall from the cliff counts as the same accident as being knocked into the river, the stand-in gets that recovery. If instead any way down from the cliff counts as a fall, the rule treats every descent the same, whatever caused it.
